question: What is the meaning of masses of materials used in buildings in relation to material information?
data_point: masses of materials used in buildings
description: The masses of materials used in buildings highlight the importance of having accurate and accessible material information. This data is crucial for assessing, promoting, and implementing circular economy principles in the construction industry. Without proper documentation and understanding of the materials' properties, quality, and quantities, it becomes challenging to reuse or recycle materials effectively, which is essential for reducing resource consumption and waste production in the building sector.

Applying these CE principles to buildings, particularly closing the 
loops, is reflected in the buildings-as-material-banks concept (Heinrich 
and Lang, 2019; Heisel and Rau-Oberhuber, 2020). Scholars argue that 
the current building stock can become a source of materials to construct 
new buildings or renovate existing ones in the future (Benachio et al., 
2020; Heinrich and Lang, 2019; Heisel and Rau-Oberhuber, 2020; Honic 
et al., 2021). This can be achieved by disassembling building products 
and materials that reach their end-of-life in one building and reusing or 
recycling them in another. Realising reuse or recycling in construction 
practices is a challenging process partly due to the lack of information 
regarding materials located in buildings (e.g., their quality, quantity, 
and properties) which is a result of insufficient documentation (Honic 
et al., 2019a; Iacovidou et al., 2018; Koutamanis et al., 2018). To 
address this information gap, the concept of material passports (MPs) 
was proposed by researchers and practitioners (e.g., Honic et al. 
(2019a); Platform CB’23 (2020)).
